terms.gloss: a cushioned chair with arms, easy chair
terms.comment: The classical word for a cushioned chair with arms (Horace, Phaedrus, Juvenal); in antiquity especially a woman’s easy chair and a teacher’s seat, whence the bishop’s cathedra. It leads here in place of Traupman’s description (Jack, 11 November 2026).
Traupman’s description, “a chair with arms”. The noun is sella, sellae f.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 122.

cathedra.against: Lewis & Short căthē^dra, a common vowel; Andresian cathēdra
cathedra.html: Greek καθέδρα, with short ε; the syllable is heavy only by position before dr, as Hor. S. 1.10.91 plōrāre cathedrās allows. A vowel Lewis & Short marks common is not a long mark.
